blocks.heading: Hotels: Cruise, Airline, Events, Your Own Kitchen

items.text: Hospitality training does not lock you into a hotel property.
Restaurant, cafe, or catering ventures are the most common self-employment path for hospitality graduates who have built real kitchen, cost-control, and guest-service experience inside a hotel first.
The hotel-operations grounding (cost control, vendor management, service standards) transfers directly into running your own place.
Ask any hospitality institute for the last two years of actual placement offers by company and role, not a headline "100% placement" claim.
Graduates who rotate through front office, F&B, and housekeeping in their first 2-3 years build the operational range that later gets them promoted to assistant manager and beyond.

Split shifts, standing for most of an 8-10 hour shift, working every major festival and weekend, and constant guest-facing energy are the real early-career workload, not a side detail buried in the job description.

visuals.heading: Salary Progression: Trainee to GM

rows: Roughly ₹15,000-₹30,000/month at branded hotels; can be lower at independent properties, often with accommodation and meals included.
Roughly ₹25,000-₹45,000/month, with faster jumps for graduates who rotate across two or more departments early.
Roughly ₹40,000-₹70,000/month; F&B and revenue management assistant managers often sit at the higher end.
Roughly ₹60,000-₹1,20,000/month at a 5-star property, often with accommodation, meals, and hotel-discount perks added on top.
Roughly ₹1.5-₹3 lakh/month at established 5-star properties, with luxury-chain GM total packages (including housing and bonus) sometimes reaching ₹40-60 lakh a year.

figures.label: Total Course Duration
figures.source: If you are weighing a hotel management career in India: entry usually happens through IHM (via NCHMCT JEE) or a private hospitality diploma, the first 2-3 years involve modest pay and genuinely long, rotating hours across front office, F&B, or housekeeping, and the payoff builds from there, department-head pay at a 5-star property, GM-level pay after roughly 15 years, or a fork into cruise lines, airlines, events, or your own F&B business once you have real operational experience behind you.

supporting: A third route exists too: some hotels, especially independent and smaller-chain properties, hire directly into entry-level operational roles without a hospitality degree at all, and promote based on performance. This route skips the debt and delay of a 3-4 year degree, but it usually caps out lower and slower than a degree-holder's ladder unless you later add formal certification or a diploma.

figures.label: Entry Level Pay
figures.source: Starting pay is genuinely modest. A management trainee typically starts around ₹15,000-₹30,000 a month at a branded hotel, sometimes less at an unbranded or independent property, though accommodation and meals often come with the role and meaningfully offset the low cash number.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: None of this means avoid hotel management, it means go in with accurate expectations. Graduates who know the first 2-3 years will be physically and socially demanding, and treat that stretch as skill-building rather than a personal failure, handle it far better than graduates who expected an easier ride.
